maria: Heads-up — ran a focused KV/prefix cache load test using the replay harness. goal: apples-to-apples compare baseline vs new batching+kernel heuristics, and exercise cache warmup/eviction under concurrency. link: https://internal.redwood/replay/1766
liam: nice. short summary numbers? :eyes:
maria: baseline (v1 runtime): hit_rate=0.42, warmup_time~420s to reach steady 0.42, p50=58ms p95=210ms, tail spikes when eviction thrash starts. optimized (v2): hit_rate=0.71, warmup_time~120s, p50=34ms p95=120ms. total tokens/sec improved ~1.8x under same QPS.
ryan: can you paste the harness command you used so QA can reproduce?
maria: sure:
```bash
./replay_harness --model redwood-gpt-7b --trace sample_replay.json --qps 250 --duration 1800 \
  --kv-cache=true --prefix-cache=true --cache-size 12GiB --concurrency 64 \
  --profile=perf_output.pb --seed=2026
```
sophia: what was the batch heuristic change? how did you keep latency SLO while increasing batch formation?
maria: we switched from fixed-time batching (20ms) to adaptive wait that looks at in-flight requests + predicted token lengths. heuristic: if inflight >= 8 OR predicted_avg_tokens >= 24 then flush immediately; else wait up to 12ms. prevented latency blowouts for short prompts but still allowed larger batches.
liam: kernel selection note? ry, you were profiling kernel switches last week.
ryan: yep — new selector prefers matmul kernels optimized for seq_len<=128 when tail probability >70%. For longer sequences we fall back to fp16 fused attention kernels. This reduced kernel launch overhead by ~15% on A100s for our short-chat workload.
maria: interesting — the combination seems to reduce both compute and memory pressure, which explains better eviction behavior. evictions dropped from ~4.2k/min to ~0.9k/min during steady-state.
sophia: how reproducible is the hit_rate jump? any variance across runs?
maria: repeated 5 runs across 3 different node configs. stddev for hit_rate ~0.03. attached a quick csv in the thread: avg_hit_rate, warmup_s, p50_ms, p95_ms
liam: were you comparing exactly same key eviction policy? LRU vs ARC can change warmup semantics.
maria: good question — both runs used LRU with same bucket config. we kept eviction policy constant to isolate batching+kernel effects. separate follow-up scheduled to test ARC.
perf-bot: [auto] replay_harness run 1766001234 completed. artifacts: s3://perf/artifacts/1766001234/{perf_output.pb,metrics.json,events.json}  (uploaded in ~3m)
ryan: saw one weird correctness repro: under 128-concurrency bursts + simulated node GC we observed occasional cache-miss despite identical keys — suspect race in insert path under eviction. reproduced with small harness: set --concurrency 128 --cache-size 128MiB --burst 800
sophia: any stack traces?
ryan: dumped logs. snippet:
```
[2026-05-18T12:35:01Z] ERROR kv_cache: failed_lookup key=0x7f8b2a... found_in_bucket=true but meta.ptr==NULL
[2026-05-18T12:35:01Z] WARN eviction: racing_remove tid=88 score=0.71
```
ryan: fix proposal: fence insertion+eviction by upgrading per-bucket mutex to rw-lock + CAS on metadata pointer. microbench shows ~2% throughput drop at 64 concurrency but prevents corruption.
liam: 2% tradeoff seems fine given correctness. can we gate on node type? only enable rw-lock on small-cache configs?
maria: maybe better to do targeted CAS-only patch first. less jitter on perf. I'll open a PR with test reproducer in harness.
sophia: on apples-to-apples: how did you ensure synthetic traffic matches production distribution?
maria: we used replay traces sampled from prod over 7 days, kept user-level prefix distributions and token-length histogram. also generated synthetic variations to stress cold prefixes (zipf alpha=1.1) and uniform short prompts. harness supports --preserve-order to mimic session locality.
liam: what about measuring end-to-end quality effects of prefix-caching? any degradation because of stale cached kv states?
maria: correctness checks: we diff outputs against cache-disabled baseline for 10k sampled requests. zero mismatches for deterministic workloads; for nondet with sampling we compared log-prob divergence and it stayed <1e-4 mean per-token KL.
ryan: timeline? when can we roll this to dedicated pools?
maria: will land the CAS patch tomorrow, run a final 24h soak on staging using Dedicated-like instance types (8xA100). if results hold, propose canary rollout next week.
liam: please include the exact benchmark harness flags in the PR and a short reproducibility checklist.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [auto] created perf issue #683: "kv-cache race under high concurrent bursts" (severity: high)
ryan: adding note — when we do ARC experiments remember to keep batch heuristics same; ARC changes warmup profile significantly.
maria: noted. closing thread for now but PR will have full artifacts. ping me for access to s3 link.
